title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-marcus-hall
body:
Sales/Partnership scratch notes - Marcus Hall

Account: NovaCloud (mid-market cloud provider)
Contact: Priya Raghavan (Head of Platform), secondary: Tom Becker (SRE lead)
Intro: came from convo at CloudInfra conf (Dec). Interested in dev-friendly inference that reduces token cost and gives predictable latency for their tenant isolation requirements.

Quick account summary:
- Industry: cloud infra / managed K8s (multi-tenant)
- ARR estimate: $10-30M
- Team size: ~120 eng, 10 infra/sre, 6 ML infra
- Current stack: self-hosted inference using local forks of OSS libs + ad-hoc autoscale (spot GPUs). Uses AWS + on-prem for regulated customers.
- Pain points: unpredictable latency on peak, high per-token inference cost, KV cache not implemented, ops overhead for model rollouts, strict data residency/compliance for some customers
- Opportunity: Dedicated offering (reserved capacity) + Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated segments. Can pitch predictable SLOs, batching + cache savings, rollout tooling.

Value props to highlight (tailored):
- Predictable latency: SLA-backed Dedicated pools -> good for their SLA commitments to customers
- Cost control: batching + prefix/KV cache -> can reduce per-token cost 20-50% depending on prompt patterns (need to run quick sample eval)
- Private deployment: VPC & on-prem options for regulated customers + KMS/HSM integration for keys
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown for billing and ops troubleshooting

Outbound email drafts (A/B test):
A) Short intro
Subject: Reduce inference ops + predictable latency for NovaCloud
Hi Priya — quick follow after CloudInfra — we help teams running customer-facing LLMs get predictable latency and 20–40% lower per-token cost via batching, KV cache, and dedicated capacity. Would love 20 minutes to share a few quick wins we’ve seen with infra teams (one was able to remove burst autoscaling for Nginx-like requests). When are you free next week?

B) More technical / tailored
Subject: Notes from CloudInfra — caching + reserved capacity for multi-tenant workloads
Priya — enjoyed our chat in the hallway. A couple quick ideas for NovaCloud: 1) reserve a Dedicated pool for steady traffic and use autoscale-burst for spikes (reduces tail latency); 2) enable prefix/KV caching for common system prompts — often yields 30% token reduction for multi-tenant prompts. Happy to run a short eval on a subset of traffic (non-prod) to estimate numbers. Thoughts?

Call script / discovery checklist:
- Confirm current inference pattern: avg tokens per request, top 10 prompts, 99th latency, cost per inference (in their metrics)
- Ask about model governance: do they pin versions? need canary rollouts?
- Data residency: which customers require on-prem vs VPC? timelines?
- Internal blockers: procurement cycles, legal review for private deployment, infra staff availability
- Win criteria: cost reduction target (%, $), latency SLOs, rollout complexity constraints

Objection handling (common + suggested responses):
- "We can just tune our infra / use spot instances" -> Acknowledge; highlight ops complexity and tail latency unpredictability. Offer a small pilot to demonstrate latency stability and cost delta vs their current spot strategy.
- "We can't onboard a vendor with customer data" -> Highlight Private deployment option (customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM support) + audit logs. If needed, propose air-gapped on-prem assessment.
- "Pricing seems unclear / too expensive" -> Position with unit economics: show per-token comparison (hosted vs current), reserved capacity amortization, and potential savings from batching/cache. Offer a structured pricing runbook for their traffic patterns (need sample traces).
- "We already have a small team building internal runtime" -> Emphasize time-to-value and engineering opportunity cost; Redwood gives same runtime guarantees + rollout/observability out of box. Offer co-build pilot where we collaborate with their engs (partnered PoC).

Quick numbers / ask for data (for a productive eval):
- sample traffic tail: 1 week of anonymized request logs (top prompts)
- tokens per request (median, p95)
- peak qps and sustained qps windows
- list of customer-regulated accounts and residency requirements

Risks / open questions:
- Procurement timeline for Private deployment (legal + security review)
- Who on their side owns infra procurement decisions? (likely Priya + platform leadership + procurement)
- Need to confirm GPU types they prefer for on-prem (A100 vs H100)

Next steps / TODOs:
- Send follow-up email with two short outbound variants (A/B) by EOD Wednesday (Olivia to review) [TODO: include bullet summary with specific ask]
- Ask Samir to prepare a quick one-pager on Dedicated pricing comps for mid-market customers (ballpark monthly commit ranges)
- Request anonymized sample logs (see "Quick numbers" list) — offer to sign NDA if needed
- Book 20-min discovery with Priya + Tom (tentative: week of Feb 24)

Notes to self (choppy):
- run quick sim: assume 1M tokens/day, if caching reduces 30% -> savings calc. Need deck slide with before/after latency distribution.
- partners? check partnership team playbook (link in linked_artifacts) for co-sell credit / referral split
- follow up: mention Redwood Optimize -> quantization + batching suggestions might be attractive given their cost focus

References / internal links:
- Confluence: infra partner playbook (see link above)
- JIRA RDWD-523: private deploy checklist (security reqs)
- GH PR: partner playbooks collab (copy for quoting examples)

End of notes.

-- Marcus
